text: Your phone needs four satellites to know where you are.
India built its own system, but for months, reportedly, only three worked.
So last night, Israel launched a fourth.
But why does India even need its own GPS?
Because a system someone else owns can be weakened or switched off.
So India built Navic, navigation with Indian constellation.
It covers India, plus about 1,500 kilometers beyond its borders.
Three of us? That's just a triangle.
Here's the catch. Your phone needs at least four to fix your spot in 3D.
Old atomic clocks failed, and in 2025, NVS-02 got stuck in the wrong orbit.
So the team of four became three.
Enter NVS-03, 2,232 kilograms, carrying an atomic clock made in India.
It's headed about 36,000 kilometers up to a parking spot above the equator.
If it works, Navic is back to 4.
So the next time your phone finds you, it might be listening to India.
3 was a crowd, 4 is a team.
